egress.terms: Served over HTTP from designated node subdomains (`node-name.radicle.garden`) without published egress metering. Peer-to-peer replication allows multiple network nodes to mirror repositories without centralized bandwidth charges.

record.tooling: `rad` CLI (Radicle heartwood), git remote `rad://`. Real client, actively developed.
record.chaining: Replication is the chaining primitive: each additional seed that follows your repo (rad id allow-list) is another free full copy and another serving endpoint. Content is addressed by git OID so it is verifiable. But it is a replication multiplier, not a capacity multiplier. Total bytes are still bounded by the largest seed.
record.limits_note: 5 GB on Garden (paid add-on beyond), per-account. Public permissive seeds are free but each sets its own cap. Fetching needs at least one node online holding the data.
record.reliability_note: Availability is the weak point, not durability: if no seed holds the repo, it is unreachable until a peer comes back. Garden states it is 'walkaway-safe'. Losing the host does not lose your local repo.
